properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: md5@2.3.0 npm dependency declared in yarn.lock (transitive dep of the TS toolchain). Ships a collision-broken hash in the build; no first-party call site found in this repo. Dependency inventory entry — the build ships it whether or not the app calls it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: First-party signature-recovery crypto: the AVM's implementation of the EVM ecrecover precompile. Fixed by the Ethereum protocol spec — the curve is not changeable here without a chain hard fork; the libsecp256k1 version/usage is.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: math/rand uses. One security-relevant use: fireblocks.go:750 Nonce: rand.Int63(), seeded at :328 with rand.Seed(time.Now().UnixNano()) — a predictable nonce in the JWT replay-protection claim sent to a custodial key service (weak PRNG in a security context). Production non-security use: batcher/queue.go:132 popRandomTx picks a random queue index (tx ordering only). The rest are random-data generators for tests/dev (common/rand.go RandBytes via math/rand.Read, inboxMessage.go:183, params.go:33, r

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RSA here is used for JWT signing (RS256 auth tokens for the Fireblocks custody API), not encryption — the eventual PQ replacement for this asset is a signature scheme (ML-DSA), not ML-KEM. Changeable here, though Fireblocks' API dictates what algorithms it will accept (observable side: a partner's stack).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Test-helper ECDSA keygen on the Ethereum curve; throwaway keys only, never used to protect production assets. Same secp256k1/ECDSA family as the AVM's C++ ecrecover implementation (ALG-673c8f24), reached here through Go.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 ECDSA across the Go stack: L2 transaction signing, wallet key derivation (cmdhelp/wallet.go), web3 account store, dev/fork-node keygen, and test keygen. Implemented through go-ethereum v1.10.18's crypto package (secp256k1 via btcsuite/btcd/btcec v2.2.0, declared in go.sum). Curve/signature scheme is fixed by the EVM protocol, so PQ migration (ML-DSA/SLH-DSA) is a protocol-level decision, not a local one. Additional sites not in the grouped list: packages/arb-rpc-node/arbostest/precompi

components.name: Go crypto/tls sessions on default settings (Go 1.13)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Two &http.Client{} constructions on Go's default crypto/tls (build targets Go 1.13-era defaults: TLS 1.2 ECDHE, no PQ key exchange). fireblocks.go:647 sends RS256-signed transaction requests to the Fireblocks custodial API — harvest-now-decrypt-later relevant. nodehealth.go:454 posts health checks to the configured OpenEthereum API. A third default-client site the collector missed (configuration.go:781, machine-blob download) is reported as a separate finding.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: tweetnacl 0.14.5 is pinned in yarn.lock and ships Ed25519 signing alongside its X25519/XSalsa20-Poly1305 surface. No first-party call site found for Ed25519 — the build ships the algorithm whether or not the application calls it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDH capability shipped via the elliptic npm package in yarn.lock (TS toolchain dependency; elliptic provides ECDH on secp256k1 among others). Dependency inventory entry; no first-party ECDH call site found in the TS sources.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: tweetnacl's scalarMult (X25519) key agreement ships in the pinned yarn.lock dependency tree. Harvest-now-decrypt-later applies if any consumer negotiates keys with it; no first-party call site found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 is the protocol hash of Ethereum (addresses, tx/message hashing, Merkle accumulators); changing it means a chain fork, not a code edit. The vendored implementation lives at packages/arb-avm-cpp/external/keccak.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory entries: golang.org/x/crypto/sha3 in packages/arb-avm-cpp/go.sum (Go side) and js-sha3 in yarn.lock (TS side) — SHA-3/Keccak implementations shipped in the build. First-party Keccak call sites are recorded under the SHA-3 in-use object (ALG-052c24b2).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2 via @ethersproject/pbkdf2 (yarn.lock:450) — part of ethers' encrypted-JSON-keystore support, alongside scrypt (ALG-c1f8b585) and AES-128-CTR via aes-js@3.0.0 (yarn.lock:427, reported separately). The TS toolchain ships keystore-encryption KDFs; quantum-safe primitive, OWASP iteration floor not visible from the lockfile.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Test exercising EVM precompile 2 (SHA-256): computes the expected digest with the Go stdlib and compares against the AVM precompile result. The production implementation it exercises is the vendored picosha2 code in machineoperation.cpp (reported as a separate finding).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/hashes provides the SHA-256 implementation in the JS dependency tree (pinned yarn.lock).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE3 via yarn.lock (TS toolchain dependency), and the same yarn.lock block (@ethersproject/json-wallets@5.6.0, line 427) pins aes-js@3.0.0 — AES-128-CTR used by ethers' encrypted-JSON-keystore encryption (Grover halves AES-128 to 64-bit security; AES-256-GCM is the PQ-era target). Hash primitive itself is Grover-weakened only; no first-party call site found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt via yarn.lock (scrypt-js / ethers keystore KDF). Memory-hard password KDF used for encrypted JSON keystores in the TS toolchain; quantum-safe, iteration/parameter strength not visible from the lockfile.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: the x/crypto/sha3 module that powers arb-util/hashing's legacy Keccak-256 also ships the SHAKE128 XOF to every Go module that imports it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: SHAKE256 XOF available through the same x/crypto/sha3 module the project imports for Keccak-256 hashing.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: tweetnacl's secretbox (XSalsa20-Poly1305 AEAD) ships in the pinned JS tree; symmetric, so only Grover-relevant, not Shor.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The JWT-signing step of the Fireblocks integration: the same unmaintained library whose RSA key parsing is confirmed at fireblocks.go:330-338. The RS256 tokens it mints are classical signatures (Shor-relevant); the library itself is unmaintained, which is a hygiene problem independent of PQ.

properties.value: CSPRNG uses, quantum-safe: datastorage.cpp:274 RAND_bytes(secret_hash_seed...) generates the machine's secret hash seed via OpenSSL's CSPRNG; precompiles_test.go:23 uses crypto/rand for test vectors. Good randomness — inventory record only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto provider inventory: golang.org/x/crypto is the Go ecosystem's extended-crypto module — it decides what kex/KDF/signature algorithms the Go services can reach (and its 2018-era pin in go.sum predates any PQ groups). The wallet.go site uses its ssh/terminal password-prompt helper; the module also feeds sha3 (legacy Keccak in arb-util/hashing) and scrypt to the tree.

properties.value: golang.org/x/crypto v0.0.0-20211215165025-cf75a172585e declared in go.mod (arb-node-core:14, arb-util:17) and pinned in go.sum — the extended Go cryptography module (SSH, sha3, ripemd160, HKDF, etc.) ships in the build. No first-party call site in this repo beyond the subpackage entries already inventoried.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: MD5 is a broken hash (collision attacks practical since 2004); this package ships it to the JS tree. Any use for integrity or auth would be CWE-328 — the inventory records its availability; downstream review decides purpose.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic pinned in yarn.lock — ECDSA/ECDH on secp256k1 (and other curves) for the TS toolchain; it is the signing backend behind ethers' wallet operations in bridge deployment/test scripts. Shor-vulnerable; migration is EVM-protocol-bound.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: golang.org/x/crypto/sha3 pinned in packages/arb-avm-cpp/go.sum — SHA-3/Keccak implementation shipped in the Go build graph (available to the Go tooling; the AVM's own Keccak is the vendored ethash C++ code).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: the 2018-era x/crypto/ssh pin negotiates only classical key exchange (curve25519-sha256, ECDH/NIST, DH groups, and the ssh-rsa SHA-1 signature path) — no PQ kex exists in that vintage, so any SSH session the tree could open is harvest-now-decrypt-later. No first-party ssh.Dial call site found; recorded as shipped capability.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes pinned in yarn.lock — audited hash library (SHA-2/SHA-3/BLAKE/ripemd) in the TS build graph; no first-party call site found.

properties.value: github.com/miekg/dns pinned in packages/arb-rpc-node/go.sum — DNS library with DNSSEC validation support, transitive dependency; the same module set pins blake256 (noted under ALG-f65301b0). No first-party DNSSEC use found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: a full JOSE stack (JWS/JWE/JWK, RSA-OAEP, ECDH-ES, AES-GCM key wrap) available to the Go tree; likely transitive (vault/api era) but shippable all the same.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Key-management infrastructure: the Vault API client is the tree's route to an external secrets/KMS service. The client itself is not a cipher, but it is the reference point for which transit/key algorithms (all classical in Vault 1.x: RSA, ECDSA P-256, ed25519, AES-GCM) the deployment can ask a Vault server to perform. No first-party call site found in this repo — recorded as integration capability.
